label: Early-sequence position unit: 3rd original token, and <DEL> in short (L<=4) sequences
explanation: Fires only near the start of a sequence. It is silent at t=0,1, fires most at t=2 (the 3rd original token, 35% of those steps, about 48% of activation mass), less at t=3 (13%), and on the <DEL> step when the sequence is short: always for L=3, 79% for L=4, rarely for L>=5. The <DEL> steps carry the largest activations (the top examples are all <DEL> after 3 tokens). It essentially never fires in the copy phase or at original positions >=4. Within t=2/3 it is token-dependent and prefers first-occurrence inputs. Rates are higher when the first token is e or z, or the previous tokens are 0/w/i/h/c/u/e, but no simple token rule separates active from inactive. That is the main source of false positives (about 65% of t=2 steps are inactive). Overall it reads as a 2-3 steps since start / early <DEL> timing signal.
